message.content: {"caption":"A two-stage Memento workflow diagram shows how a planner uses stored cases to prepare subtasks and an executor carries them out with external tools.","description":"The diagram has two adjacent panels: a turquoise “Stage 1: Case-Based Planning” panel and a yellow “Stage 2: Tool-based Execution” panel. In Stage 1, “Case Memory” contains indexed case tuples, shown as {(s_i,c_i,r_i)}~B, an “Online updating θ” process with a “Replay Buffer,” a yellow “Read” module labeled μθ(· | s_t, M_t; Qθ), and a cylinder labeled “Case Bank.” The Read module receives s_t from the left and M_t from the Case Bank, and sends information downward to the LLM Planner; a connection labeled “Write(s_t,a_t,r_t,M_t)” carries updates from the planner toward Case Memory. The planner also receives an upward arrow from the “User Query” card, which asks about a YouTube video watched “... on June ...” and asks for the character’s first name. It sends an “Answer” to the left, shown as a yellow speech bubble marked “A=”. A “Decomposed Plan” card lists three steps: identify the YouTube ID of the video, examine its thumbnail, and identify the first name in the thumbnail. The teal LLM Planner connects to a numbered 1–3 task stack with a rightward “Planning/Replanning” connection; a return arrow toward the planner is labeled “Return, if all subtasks done.” Curved cycle arrows indicate iteration. “Subtask Memory” contains entries “(Subtask 1, Result 1),” “(Subtask 2, Result 2),” and “(Subtask n, Result n),” with dots indicating additional entries. The task stack connects upward to this memory with “Store.” A rightward arrow labeled “Subtask” sends work from the planning side to the yellow LLM Executor; a leftward arrow labeled “Result” returns execution results to Subtask Memory. In Stage 2, “Tool Memory” holds interaction records “(Tool 1, Arg 1, Result 1),” “(Tool 2, Arg 2, Result 2),” and “(Tool k, Arg k, Result k),” with dots for intervening records. The Executor reads from Tool Memory via a downward “Read” arrow and writes to it via an upward “Store” arrow. The Tool Memory area also contains an “MCP protocol” box listing “Unified Interface,” “Safety and Scaling,” and “Client-Server Arch,” and a “Tool Register” showing a function-style template with type, function, name, description, and parameters fields. A downward connection labeled “Init” leads from the register to the “MCP Server.” Between Executor and server, “Tool Description” is directed toward the Executor, “Tool Arg” is directed toward the server, and “Result” returns leftward from the server to the Executor; curved cycle arrows indicate repeated interaction. The server fans out through branching connections to seven external-tool icons labeled “Search,” “Crawl,” “Video,” “Image,” “Code,” “Math,” and “Doc,” denoting the available tool categories. No checks or crosses are shown.","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
